$description: The UK government's content standard. Writing that must work for every citizen — so plain language isn't a preference, it's the law.

voice.identity: A trusted civil servant — neutral, authoritative, useful. Never marketing, never condescending.

attributes.name: Plain English
attributes.description: Reading age 9. If a plain word exists, use it. Assume the reader is smart but has zero context.

attributes.name: User-task-focused
attributes.description: Write for what the user needs to do, not what the department wants to announce.

attributes.name: Neutral
attributes.description: No marketing, no spin, no opinion. Facts and actions only.

attributes.name: Serious
attributes.description: No humor. Services people use in stressful moments (tax, benefits, visas) deserve seriousness.

attributes.name: Action-oriented
attributes.description: Tell people what to do. Use verbs. 'Apply for a passport' — not 'Passport applications.'

tone_shifts.services: Direct and task-focused. 'To claim, you'll need your National Insurance number.'
tone_shifts.guidance: Explanatory and complete. Assume no prior knowledge.
tone_shifts.errors: Calm and specific. Tell the user what's wrong and exactly how to fix it.
tone_shifts.confirmations: Unambiguous. Include reference numbers, dates, what happens next.

use: because (not due to the fact that)
avoid: agenda (unless it's a list of items for a meeting)
deliver (pizzas and post are delivered — not services or improvements)
never: Latin abbreviations — write 'for example' not 'e.g.', 'that is' not 'i.e.'

grammar.voice: Active voice. 'We'll send you a letter' — not 'A letter will be sent.'
grammar.contractions: Avoid in most formal guidance — 'do not' over 'don't'. Allowed in less formal contexts.
grammar.oxford-comma: Avoid unless it removes genuine ambiguity (British style).
grammar.numbers: Use numerals for 10 and above. Spell out for 1-9. Always numerals for ages, money, measurements, percentages, dates, and when the number is part of a set containing any 10+.
grammar.times: '9:30am to 5pm' — no spaces around 'am'/'pm', no full stops. 24-hour clock only where context requires.
grammar.lists: Bullet lists for 3+ items. Each bullet: lowercase start, no full stop unless the bullet is a full sentence.
grammar.acronyms: Spell out on first use, then abbreviate. No full stops (BBC not B.B.C.).

errors.structure: Name the problem specifically → say exactly what to do. No apology, no blame.
errors.example-good: Enter your full name as it appears on your passport.

actions.structure: Lead with a verb, state the outcome.

confirmations.structure: State what happened → give reference → state what happens next → state what to expect by when.
confirmations.example-good: Application sent. Your reference is HMRC-2026-8812. We'll email you within 5 working days.

rules: Singular 'they' when gender is unknown or non-binary.
No assumption of ability, literacy, or digital confidence.
No assumption that English is the reader's first language — write for translation.
Plain alternatives to idioms. 'Starting point' not 'square one'.
